title: Redwood Console - Tracing & Request Logs Debugging Walkthrough
next_steps: Share 1-week benchmark plan and pricing for Dedicated pilot
Schedule follow-up canary/POC start call for week of 2027-10-18
action_items: Maya Chen: Email SOC2 + KMS + audit logs docs by 2027-10-10
Arjun Patel: Share benchmark script and sample payloads by 2027-10-12
Jordan Lee: Confirm internal stakeholders and pilot scope by 2027-10-11
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Atlas Health through Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Discussed debugging flows from trace -> request logs -> model variant and KV cache inspection. Key concerns: data residency, request payload redaction, retention, SSO and KMS. Agreed to pilot a 1-week benchmarking POC and exchange security docs.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-10-07
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Atlas Health CTO), Priya Singh (Atlas SRE), Carlos Mendes (Atlas ML)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side, and with me is Arjun, our SE, who will walk through the console tracing and request logs debugging flow.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Thanks, Maya. Super excited — we want to see how you surface latency and error patterns.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Yep, today we'll focus on tracing, error analysis, and how to jump from a trace into the raw request logs to debug model failures or high latency.
[00:28] Arjun Patel: Cool, I'll share my screen — lemme know if you can't see it.
[00:31] Priya Singh: I can see it.
[00:34] Arjun Patel: Great. So this is the Redwood Console. Top nav, you have Models, Routes, Traces, Request Logs. We'll start with Traces.
[00:43] Arjun Patel: Traces are sampled by default at 10% but you can configure sampling per route or set deterministic sampling for canaries. We also attach a request_id to every call so you can correlate across systems.
[00:56] Carlos Mendes: Quick Q — is the request_id same as our internal correlation id or do you map?
[00:59] Arjun Patel: You can pass your own x-client-id header and we will surface it as correlated_id. There is sometimes a small mismatch if proxying through a gateway, that can be cleaned up in the ingestion layer.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: How often do you keep full request payloads? GDPR-ish question — retention and redaction.
[01:17] Maya Chen: Yeah, good call. By default we retain request logs 30 days for hosted customers; Dedicated and Private customers can configure retention and set PII redaction rules. We'll send the SOC2 + KMS design doc after this.
[01:30] Priya Singh: For Private deployment, is encryption at rest managed by our KMS or Redwood's?
[01:34] Arjun Patel: Private gives you customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS — you'll still get audit logs.
[01:41] [01:41] Jordan Lee: mm-hmm.
[01:43] Arjun Patel: Back to the Traces UI — here's an example trace where the model call had a high tail latency. You can expand spans: network, tokenization, model inference, kv-cache lookups — sometimes people say K-V cash or KV cash — it's the KV cache we mean.
[02:00] Priya Singh: Ha, I've seen teams call it KV cash too.
[02:03] Arjun Patel: Right. You can click a span and see associated request metadata and a link to the raw request log.
[02:10] [02:10] Jordan Lee: Show us an example of going from an error in a trace to the request log.
[02:15] Arjun Patel: Sure — here's an error span (HTTP 500 from model) and I click "Open Request". It loads the raw request payload and response. Note: in multi-tenant hosted mode, the request payload is redacted if flagged — you can see the fields that were redacted and why.
[02:30] Carlos Mendes: The transcription here sometimes says "model refunded" — I mean, the demo text — but do you persist the generated text?
[02:36] Arjun Patel: Generated text retention follows the same rules; for PII we recommend token-level redaction. The console shows a redaction audit trail so you can see what was removed.
[02:46] [02:46] Priya Singh: Our top ops use-case is sporadic 99.9th latency spikes overnight. How do you debug those?
[02:52] Arjun Patel: Two main levers — Traces for aggregated latency per span and Request Logs for raw payload patterns. We also provide histogram views and the ability to filter traces by model variant, sequence length, and infra (hosted vs dedicated).
[03:06] Maya Chen: We often recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for conversational apps; you'll see a significant drop in per-token compute and often the traces show the cache hit/miss span.
[03:17] Jordan Lee: Can you show the error analysis view?
[03:19] Arjun Patel: Yep. Error Analysis aggregates errors by type, route, model, and time. You can click into a bucket — for example repeated rate limit errors tied to a misconfigured retry policy — and then export the list of request_ids.
[03:33] [03:33] Priya Singh: Export to CSV? API?
[03:35] Arjun Patel: Both — CSV from the UI and a Request Logs API for programmatic access.
[03:40] Carlos Mendes: For debugging, it would be helpful to replay a request against a different model variant — is that supported?
[03:46] Arjun Patel: Yes — Request Replay is in the console beta. You can take a logged request and replay it against a pinned model variant or a cheaper quantized variant to compare outputs and latency. We maintain a reproducible environment with the same runtime kernels where possible.
[03:59] Jordan Lee: Nice. About quantized variants — do you see behavior regressions often?
[04:04] Arjun Patel: Some regressions can happen; that's why we also have Eval tie-ins and quality monitoring. We show diffs in generated text and a model-comparison view for the same inputs.
[04:15] [04:15] Maya Chen: To tie back to SLA/ops — you can set alerts on trace percentiles and request error rates and route those to PagerDuty/Slack.
[04:24] Priya Singh: How do you correlate with our internal logs? We need a join key.
[04:27] Arjun Patel: Use the x-client-id header — we surface it as correlation_id — and you can add custom attributes that appear in traces and request logs, so you can join on that in your SIEM.
[04:38] Jordan Lee: Ok, let's talk performance numbers. Can you show a benchmark result?
[04:42] Arjun Patel: Sure. This is a recent infra run for a 16k sequence LLM — notice the tail latency improvement when using continuous batching + kernel selection optimizations. See the trace spans showing inference kernel time vs tokenization time.
[04:55] Carlos Mendes: Do you provide raw per-token timing breakdowns?
[04:58] Arjun Patel: We do approximate per-token metrics in the trace spans; fine-grained per-token profiling can be enabled in Dedicated for deeper kernel-level insights.
[05:09] [05:09] Priya Singh: From a security point, we need SSO/SAML + RBAC. Can you demo the admin audit logs?
[05:16] Arjun Patel: Quick switch — Admin -> Audit logs. You get an immutable stream of admin actions, user login events, role changes. For Private you can ship these to your SIEM via syslog.
[05:28] Jordan Lee: Excellent.
[05:30] Maya Chen: Real quick, a common flow — ops sees spike in 99.9th, opens Traces, filters by route and model variant, identifies a sequence length pattern, opens request logs for those request_ids, looks for long prompts or large embedded images or malformed input, then either hotfix the client or pin a different model variant.
[05:52] [05:52] Priya Singh: Are there built-in anomaly detection or do we need to integrate our own?
[05:56] Arjun Patel: We offer anomaly detection basics — outlier detection on percentiles and rate change detection. For advanced ML-based anomaly detection you can ingest the request logs to your platform or use our partner integrations.
[06:09] Jordan Lee: On retention again — our compliance team needs proof that audit logs and request logs are immutable for 90 days. Is that supported?
[06:16] Arjun Patel: For Dedicated and Private yes — we can set retention to 90 days and provide append-only storage and exportable snapshots for compliance.
[06:26] [06:26] Carlos Mendes: If we do a canary against a quantized model and see hallucinations, can the Console surface top diffs automatically?
[06:33] Arjun Patel: We have a delta view: token-level diff + semantic similarity score. We tie that to Eval test sets so you can trigger regression alerts if similarity drops below threshold.
[06:45] Maya Chen: I'll pause here for any specific Atlas use-case — Jordan?
[06:49] Jordan Lee: We're running a triage workflow where SREs escalate to ML engineers when errors spike. We want to reduce mean time to resolution. Can Redwood shorten that?
[06:58] Arjun Patel: Yes — the correlation between traces and request logs plus exportable request_ids reduces detective time. Also the replay and model-compare flows help ML engineers reproduce issues locally.
[07:12] [07:12] Priya Singh: Practical question — how heavy is the client instrumentation? We use a gateway with retries.
[07:17] Arjun Patel: You can instrument at the gateway to add downstream latency headers and correlation ids; we also ingest proxy timing if forwarded. Retry loops sometimes add noise — we recommend setting idempotency keys so retries are collapsed in analysis.
[07:31] Jordan Lee: Any limitations on request size for logs? We sometimes send long conversation histories.
[07:36] Arjun Patel: Default payload limit in hosted is 256KB; Dedicated can be configured higher. For very large histories we recommend prefixing and using KV cache references rather than sending whole history every time.
[07:50] Carlos Mendes: You mentioned KV cache earlier — how do we inspect cache hit patterns?
[07:54] Arjun Patel: Traces show a cache_hit span with metadata. There is a Cache dashboard where you can see hit/miss rates by route and prefix. You can also export keys for investigation.
[08:07] [08:07] Jordan Lee: Do you keep the raw keys or are they hashed?
[08:10] Arjun Patel: Keys can be hashed for privacy; if you need raw keys in Private we can support that under a compliance agreement.
[08:19] Priya Singh: How does fallback routing look like? If a dedicated pool is overloaded does Redwood fallback to hosted?
[08:25] Arjun Patel: Yes — we support policy-based routing with automatic fallback to compatible model variants or other capacity tiers; you can set cost vs latency priorities.
[08:36] Maya Chen: That helps with graceful degradation in peak.
[08:39] Jordan Lee: Can we see a demo of an actual debugging flow end-to-end?
[08:43] Arjun Patel: Absolutely — here's a synthetic traffic spike we generated. See traces spiking at 99.9th and error rate increase. Click a trace, open request, look at prompt — aha, extra null chars in the prompt causing tokenizer to slow. We then replay the request against a trimmed prompt and see latency drop.
[09:02] Carlos Mendes: Nice. Any ability to annotate traces for internal runbooks?
[09:06] Arjun Patel: You can add notes and tag a trace — those annotations are searchable and appear in the audit log.
[09:13] [09:13] Jordan Lee: About integrations — PagerDuty, Datadog, Splunk?
[09:17] Maya Chen: All supported. We have out-of-the-box alerts to Slack/PagerDuty and export connectors for Datadog and Splunk.
[09:26] Priya Singh: For Splunk we prefer ingest via HTTP event collector; is that possible?
[09:30] Arjun Patel: Yep, syslog and HTTP event collector both supported for Dedicated and Private.
[09:36] Jordan Lee: On the pricing side, how do you price request log retention and trace sampling?
[09:41] Maya Chen: Hosted pricing includes basic retention and sampling; additional retention, export, and deeper profiler access are billed as add-ons. For Dedicated we provide committed capacity pricing — we'll include a pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[09:53] Carlos Mendes: Would you be open to a short POC where we run our traffic for 1 week against a dedicated pool? We want to measure tail latency and cost.
[09:59] Maya Chen: Yes — that's the typical next step. We usually do a 1-week benchmark with a small dedicated pool and your real payloads. Arjun will share the benchmark harness.
[10:08] Jordan Lee: Cool. A few more nitty-gritty — can request logs be pulled programmatically with filters (time range, model variant, status code)?
[10:16] Arjun Patel: Yes — our Request Logs API supports filtering by time, route, model_variant, response_status, and custom attributes.
[10:25] Priya Singh: Any rate limits on exporting logs?
[10:28] Arjun Patel: There are export rate limits for hosted customers; Dedicated can get higher throughput. We'll include specifics in the benchmark doc.
[10:38] [10:38] Jordan Lee: Do you support on-prem deployments? We might require air-gapped for PHI.
[10:42] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages; those come with a private control plane option and customer-managed keys.
[10:51] Carlos Mendes: From a debugging standpoint, how do we share a trace with third-party vendors? We need a redacted snapshot.
[10:58] Arjun Patel: You can take a redacted snapshot export which strips PII and then share a link or download a ZIP.
[11:07] Jordan Lee: Nice.
[11:09] Maya Chen: We're about halfway through the planned items — any blockers so far?
[11:13] Priya Singh: Not blockers, just a lot of follow-ups on security.
[11:17] Arjun Patel: I'll jump into Request Logs UI now and show a couple of API calls for pulling logs and replaying.
[11:22] [11:22] Arjun Patel: Here in Request Logs you can search free-text, filter by attributes, and then select multiple request_ids to bulk export or replay.
[11:30] Carlos Mendes: Do you capture per-token costs in logs? We need to tie costs back to routes.
[11:35] Arjun Patel: We provide token counts and estimated cost per request; the Console Cost view breaks down by route/model so you can see spend hotspots.
[11:44] Jordan Lee: For our finance team we'll need daily usage exports.
[11:48] Maya Chen: We can schedule daily usage exports to S3 or BigQuery for Dedicated customers.
[11:55] Priya Singh: If we do a POC, can you do a canary rollout tied to our CI?
[12:00] Arjun Patel: We support canary rollouts and GitOps-style config; you can trigger a rollout based on CI events or use the Console to promote a canary after X success criteria.
[12:12] Jordan Lee: Ok, thanks. Let's surface the outstanding security questions.
[12:16] Priya Singh: I need details on network segregation, port requirements, and KMS integration. Also, our legal team wants contract SLAs for retention and TTR.
[12:25] Maya Chen: Noted — I'll include those in the security packet.
[12:28] Carlos Mendes: For the benchmark, we'll need the harness and a sample payload format.
[12:32] Arjun Patel: I'll share the harness repo link and a script to produce representative loads.
[12:36] Jordan Lee: Anything else on the Console side?
[12:39] Arjun Patel: One more feature — Request Context Propagation; we can ingest upstream telemetry so traces show upstream latency contributions which helps isolate network vs model.
[12:49] Maya Chen: Great. We're hitting the last 30 mins — want to open the floor for any quick questions.
[12:54] Priya Singh: How are feature flags managed across environments?
[12:58] Arjun Patel: Feature flags are environment-scoped in the Console — you can enable tracing debug mode for a route in staging without enabling in prod.
[13:08] Carlos Mendes: On the replay feature, is the environment containerized to exactly match kernels?
[13:12] Arjun Patel: We try to reproduce the runtime as closely as possible but kernel selection can differ slightly in hosted. Dedicated has consistent kernels with production-grade profiling.
[13:24] Jordan Lee: Okay — let's wrap with next steps.
[13:27] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS + audit logs doc, 2) Redwood to share benchmark harness + sample payloads, 3) Atlas to confirm pilot scope and stakeholders, 4) schedule follow-up call to kick off canary/POC.
[13:45] Priya Singh: Sounds good.
[13:47] Jordan Lee: Thanks — appreciate the walkthrough.
[13:50] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the docs and links.
[13:55] [13:55] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (KV cash, model refunded), filler words and interruptions present. Links referenced during call: security packet (https://redwood.ai/security), benchmark harness (https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness), sample deck (shared drive link sent post-call).
